Figure 2:Overview of PINE.The point, normal and instance streams embed their maps with the frozen DINOv3 features and pass through DiT blocks as one sequence.
In attention, the stream mask decides which streams interact, ray positions encode the intrinsics and grounding attention adds the DINOv3 affinity.
Each stream decodes its own map, and one step at inference gives all three maps.

Figure 3:Camera-aware ray encoding.(a) The positionρj\rho_{j}of tokenjjis the point where its ray meets the image plane of a reference camera.
(b) With ray positions, a zoomed crop lands inside the full view, and the point at the red cross keeps one position.
(c) With patch indices, the crop has its own grid and gives the same point a second position.

Figure 4:Grounding attention.Each row shows an image and the attention of the query patch at the red cross, without and with grounding attention.
Grounding attention keeps the attention on the region of the query patch.

Figure 5:Qualitative comparison on point maps, depth, normals and instances.The red dot marks the point prompt of each instance.
Arrows highlight the regions we significantly improved.

Figure 6:Lateral and depth error with and without the camera-aware ray encoding.(a) Input image with five marked pixels on one row. (b) Top view of the points of this row. Each arrow points from the ground-truth point of a marked pixel to its predicted point. (c) The error of pixel 2, split into a lateral partεx​y\varepsilon_{xy}and a depth partεz\varepsilon_{z}.
Figure 10:Point error with and without the camera-aware ray encoding.Top: input image and predicted depth. Bottom: ground-truth depth and point error maps.

Figure 12:Attention with and without grounding attention.Each row shows the image, the attention of the query patch without and with grounding attention, and their difference.
The cross marks the query patch, and the contour marks its region.
Figure 13:Point maps (1/3).For each image, the first row shows the input and the predicted point maps, and the second row shows the ground-truth point map and the point error map of each method.
Figure 14:Point maps (2/3).For each image, the first row shows the input and the predicted point maps, and the second row shows the ground-truth point map and the point error map of each method.
Figure 15:Point maps (3/3).For each image, the first row shows the input and the predicted point maps, and the second row shows the ground-truth point map and the point error map of each method.
Figure 16:Depth.For each image, the first row shows the input and the predicted depth maps, and the second row shows the ground-truth depth and the depth error map of each method.
Figure 17:Surface normals.For each image, the first row shows the input and the predicted normals, and the second row shows the ground-truth normals and the angular error map of each method.

Figure 18:Planarity on iBims-1.Each row shows the input and, for the ground truth and each method, the signed distance of each point to the plane fitted to its annotated plane region. Red and blue mark the two sides of the plane, and gray marks pixels outside the planes.
Figure 19:Point-prompted instances (1/2).Each row shows the input with its point prompt, the ground-truth instance and the masks of SAM, gen2seg and PINE for the same prompt.
Figure 20:Point-prompted instances (2/2).Each row shows the input with its point prompt, the ground-truth instance and the masks of SAM, gen2seg and PINE for the same prompt.
